LWS 501.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 501.description: Integration of soil physics, chemistry, and biology in understanding essential soil processes. Equivalency: SOIL_V 501. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 510.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 510.description: Current and emerging issues relevant within the general context of land and water systems, and the significance of professional credibility and exposure. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 515.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 515.description: Watershed evaluation, key aspects of hydrology, water quality, land use impacts on water resources and integration of multiple land use activities and their cumulative impacts. Equivalency: SOIL_V 515. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 516.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 516.description: Urbanization impacts on water resources with a focus on rainwater management, water quality, point and non-point sources of pollution, drinking water and waste water, riparian buffer zones, cumulative effects, and application of beneficial management practices. Equivalency: SOIL_V 516. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 517.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 517.description: Topics in land and water system evaluations and assessing resource development options: monitoring and modelling environmental systems. Equivalency: SOIL_V 517. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 520.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 520.description: Intensive and extensive agriculture with a focus on water needs, water use, and impacts on water resources. Non-point sources of pollution, nutrient modelling, soil and land degradation, protection, and rehabilitation of watersheds including buffer zones, wetlands, and best management practices. Equivalency: SOIL_V 520. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 525.course_name: Global Issues in Land and Water Systems
LWS 525.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 525.description: Historical framework of importance of water basins, legacy between water basins and human evolution, effects of agriculture, forestry, industry and urbanization. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 530.course_name: Directed Studies in Land and Water Systems
LWS 530.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 530.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 548.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 548.description: Professional paper on topics focusing on emerging issues in water and land resources. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

LWS 550.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
LWS 550.description: Communication strategies for natural resource management professionals, with an emphasis on written, oral and digital media communications in a multi-stakeholder context. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
